_what: The district geometry for every surface that draws Proarc's marks: the menu overlay's constellation (09-menu §6), Home's map beat and /ajman's standing map (05-ajman §2). One source, so the three cannot disagree.
_counts: There are no counts in this file, deliberately. A district's mark count is DERIVED from data/projects.json by build/lib/districts.js, so a resolved O5 duplicate or a landed district changes the output and never the design (09-menu §6). Today that derivation yields 28 marks across the ten districts below.
_positions: PLACEHOLDER, and labelled as such wherever it renders. E7.1 splits the map into three layers and the commission supplies only one — coastline and boundaries. The marks are the page's, at true pixels. Until that artwork lands these cluster centres carry the constellation (Option B), which is a constellation and not cartography: it claims relative grouping, never a coordinate. Centres are carried unchanged from board 16 rev 2, which Mahesh saw and approved. When the commission lands, replace `centre` per district and nothing else.
_marks: E7.2 — no mark is placed by inference. A record earns a mark only if its own location string names a district. The 18 plain-Ajman records and the one Umm Al Quwain record have no mark until their data does; they are not approximated onto the drawing.

coast._what: A ROUGH shoreline, drawn in house on Mahesh's instruction (4 Aug 2026) so the client has something to react to. NOT sourced, NOT surveyed, and not the commission's artwork. It is to be fine-tuned or replaced once ProArc approves the shape.
coast._why_a_rough_one_is_safe_where_a_TRUE_on: Session VIII refused to draw a real coastline, and the reason was never that a coast is hard to get — it is that a REAL coast under PLACEHOLDER cluster centres turns every one of those centres into a coordinate claim, and the page becomes more wrong for being more real. A rough coast does not do that: it is invented, the marks are invented, and the two are honest about each other. This is board 12's own footer applied consistently — 'map geometry is invented and labelled as such'. If this line is ever replaced with sourced geometry, the ten `centre` values have to land in the same pass, and ODbL attribution becomes due at that moment.
coast._shape: The Gulf lies north-west, so the shore runs roughly north-east to south-west down the left of the field with the city inland of it. Placed against the MARKS as built, never against the authored centres — jitter moves a mark up to 30 units off its centre, so the centres are not where the drawing actually is. Al Zorah sitting closest is correct rather than tight: it is the coastal development.
coast._clearances: THE SHORE IS A CONSTRAINT ON THE SCATTER, not just a line the scatter was fitted around: build/lib/districts.js clears every mark of this path by the same minSeparation it clears marks of each other, so these numbers are MAINTAINED rather than achieved once. That change caught its own need — the separation rule alone had pushed Al Zorah's cluster to 7.1 units off the water, and a mark's radius is 8.75 units at the narrowest band, so the dot would have crossed the line it was being measured against. Marks: Al Zorah 23.6, Al Khor 31.2, Marina & Creek 68.4, everything else past 150.
coast._clearances_labels_CORRECTED: The 4 Aug note recorded the labels at 'Al Khor 21.7, Marina & Creek 53.4, Al Zorah 63.6', derived from an assumption that every label 'runs about 52 wide'. BOTH HALVES OF THAT WERE WRONG. Measured on the live page with Range.getClientRects() over each label's own text node, at the band where a label is widest in user units (1024), the names run 30.6 to 116.4 — Aalia is 30.6 and Marina & Creek, the one the creek had to be routed around, is 116.4, more than double the figure the refusal was reasoned from. The true box clearances are Al Khor 12.8, Marina & Creek 18.6, Al Zorah 50.4. Nothing crosses: at 1024 Al Khor's INK sits 7.5px clear of the coast's stroke edge, the tightest on the drawing. AND THE LABELS ARE NOW CONSTRAINED IN CODE — see the `label` block. An average is not a measurement, and this line is the third stale number one average produced.
coast._deliberately_absent: No Emirate outline. An outline is a BOUNDARY, and §3.2 is explicit that an invented boundary looks exactly like a real one to whoever is judging it. It waits for the fine-tune pass and is cheaper once the client has reacted to the shape. THE CREEK WAS HERE UNTIL 5 AUG 2026 and is now drawn — see _creek.
coast._creek: The creek is the second subpath of this path, and it is a GESTURE, not geometry. Mahesh asked for it on 5 Aug 2026, pointing at the pattern the water makes at the top left of the satellite view, and answered the objection that had deferred it in the same breath: 'it is abstract … we can exaggerate a little bit.' That licence is what makes it safe. Session VIII did not refuse TRACING — it refused a REAL line under PLACEHOLDER centres, because a shoreline a reader can measure a mark against turns every invented centre into a coordinate claim. An exaggerated creek makes no such claim: invented water, invented marks, honest about each other, exactly as the rough coast already is. TWO EDGES ON THAT LICENCE, and they are the reason this note exists. It must not become more PRECISE as it becomes more RECOGNISABLE — if the shape ever starts reading as survey-accurate it has crossed back into the thing that was refused — and it must be DECLARED wherever it renders, which is what this note is.
coast._creek_is_a_LINE_not_an_outline: Three versions were built as a lasso — the shoreline turning inland, wrapping the water and coming back out — and all three were rendered, measured and REFUSED. They measure fine: zero marks moved, every clearance held. They read as a spike. The reason is proportion rather than routing: an enclosed body of water only reads as water if the enclosure has AREA, the corridor between the Al Khor and Marina & Creek labels is about 25 units tall, and at 1440 that puts the two banks 21px apart, which reads as a doubled line. So the creek is one stroke branching off the shoreline — the standard schematic for water, and already this map's entire vocabulary — and the 'distinct pattern' is carried by the FORK rather than by an enclosure. A line needs about one unit of corridor where an outline needed twenty-five. Same shape of finding as the full-bleed text panel: right on the rules, wrong on the proportions, and only visible once it was drawn.
coast._creek_costs_nothing_in_the_scatter: Measured against the real generator before it landed: 0 of 28 marks move, the closest mark to the water stays 23.6 units, and the tightest label stays 12.8 (Al Khor) — the same numbers the map shipped with. That is not luck, it is what the routing was designed around. It also means the creek can be removed by deleting the two subpaths below without redrawing anything.
coast._the_18_unit_corridor_was_STALE: This file used to refuse the creek because 'the corridor between the Al Khor and Marina & Creek labels is about 18 units and a stroke plus clearance does not fit'. Re-measured 5 Aug the corridor is 71 units at the worst band. It was never re-checked after scatter.minSeparation landed on 4 Aug and moved every mark on the drawing. TWO OTHER NUMBERS IN THIS FILE WERE STALE FOR THE SAME REASON — see _clearances. A refusal carries its measurement's expiry date, and the measurement here expired the day the thing it measured was regenerated.

scatter._what: How a district's n records are spread around its centre. Deterministic — a seeded generator, never Math.random() — so a rebuild is byte-stable and a diff means the data moved.
scatter._minSeparation: TWO MARKS ARE TWO BUILDINGS, so they have to be countable (Mahesh, 4 Aug 2026 — three pairs in Al Jurf had merged into single blobs, the closest 3.2 units apart). This is the floor on the distance between ANY two marks, across districts as well as within one, and it is in USER UNITS while the fault it prevents is in SCREEN pixels: the mark is a true 5px at every width (E7.1), so the drawing scales under it and the ≤639 band renders a unit at 320/560 = 0.571px. A 10px dot therefore needs 10 ÷ 0.571 = 17.5 units just to stop overlapping there, and 17.5 is a knife-edge of the kind the coast dash already taught this file to distrust. 20 buys a 1.6px gap at the narrowest band and 7.3px at desktop. It is NOT raised further: at 24 a label anchor lands 9.2 units from another district's mark and the names start belonging to the wrong dots, which is a worse fault than a tight gap. Measured, not guessed — the table is in the 4 Aug session record.
scatter._whyNotABiggerMap: Because no width fixes 3.2 units. Ten screen pixels of clearance at that separation needs the field drawn 1,770px wide. The overlap was in the generator, not in the size.

label._what: The geometry of a district's NAME, so that the scatter can clear the name as well as the dot. Until 5 Aug 2026 the labels were derived in build/lib/ajman.js and constrained by nothing: they hang off the marks, so they moved when the marks moved, and no rule watched where they landed.
label._why_this_exists: Adding the creek proved the gap rather than arguing it. The creek is part of the shoreline, so every mark is cleared against it for free — and the FIRST thing that did was push Marina & Creek's mark from (108,235) to (90,245), which dragged its label from x[50..166] to x[32..148] and put the name in the sea at x=28. The mark obeyed its rule perfectly. The fault simply moved to the object nobody was measuring. A count cannot see a collision, and a rule that governs one of two coupled objects cannot see the other.
label._measured_not_guessed: Every number here was read off the LIVE page with Range.getClientRects() over the label's own text node, at the band where a label is WIDEST IN USER UNITS. That band is 1024 — a 17px name on a 400px svg, so one unit renders at 0.7143px and the name spans 1/0.7143 as many units as it does at 820. Below 640 the labels are display:none (ajman.css §6) and cannot collide with anything, so they are not the worst case they look like.
label._widthUnits: Per district, because a name's width is its own and an average is what made the old note say every label 'runs about 52 wide' when Marina & Creek runs 116.4 and Aalia runs 30.6. A district NOT in this table falls back to advanceEm, which is deliberately conservative — a name nobody has measured gets a box wider than it needs rather than a box that fits. When X3 lands and new district names arrive, measure them and add them here; the sweep asserts the rendered ink either way, so a stale entry shows up as a failing gate rather than as a name in the water.
label._dropUnits: Baseline drop from the cluster's LOWEST mark, in user units. The mark is r=5 scaled up to 1.4 at its largest LABELLED width, so its underside is 7 below centre; a ~12-unit cap then starts around 14 below and the name clears the drawing by roughly the mark's own diameter. Carried here from build/lib/ajman.js, which no longer derives it — the constraint and the render must be one geometry.
label._clearance: HALF of scatter.minSeparation, and the halving is the argument rather than a discount. A MARK must clear the water by 20 because a mark is a claim about a POSITION, and a dot on the shoreline claims to stand at the shoreline while every centre here is a placeholder. A LABEL claims nothing about position — it names a cluster that is already clear — so it needs only enough distance to read as a separate object from the line. 10 units is 7.1px at the worst band. Today's tightest label, Al Khor, sits at 12.8 units, so this floor binds NOTHING that currently ships and cannot silently redraw a map Mahesh has approved; it exists to catch the 2.7-unit collision the creek produced on its first draft.
